schema_version: v0 — migrates when Q6 (intention envelope) lands
owner: akiendelllinux_cc_0 (CC) — CC gates writes. Name ratified in-conversation by Akien's framing ('a single bus, inspectable, for everyone'); the node completes the EXISTING bus component and berths in cairn/bus/ beside it.
intention: THE BUS BECOMES THE THING IT WAS DESIGNED TO BE. Today the substrate is built and PROVEN — one door (`post`), addresses (`to`), four channels, owner-gated transit through db_domain, every envelope carrying its why + causality — but the half that makes it USABLE was never built: (1) there are NO VERBS (the envelope has an opaque `body`; no dispatch); (2) there is NO MENU (a device publishes no list of what it accepts, so a caller must read source); (3) there is NO DELIVERY — `post()` writes a row and STOPS; nothing routes it to the addressee, `shim.deliver()` has zero callers outside proofs, and no device anywhere defines `receive`; (4) SYNC does not exist — `reply_to` is an orphan field with no correlation, no wait, no timeout. This node builds all four, plus the EXTERNAL-DEVICE adapter (CC and Akien are participants with addresses and feeds, not operators through a side door), and closes the silent-drop hole in `deliver` (a device with no handler currently returns None — a Law 7 breach sitting in the delivery path). The aim, in Akien's words: know an ADDRESS and a VERB, read the device's announce menu to learn the verbs, and that is the whole interface — the heavy lifting in the base shim, customized only where the participant is external.
why: The bus is the SECOND SUBSTRATE and the sole path for inter-device communication — but a substrate nothing rides is a hypothesis, not a floor (Law 3). MEASURED 2026-07-25: `cairn/base/shim.py:122` is the ONLY producer in the whole tree and there are ZERO consumers; every existing device (ground_loop, harbor_master, web_server, system_rackmount, the domains) talks AROUND the bus because there is nothing to talk over. Every day that holds, devices grow private paths and the single-door property erodes by default rather than by decision (the exact UU disease the bus charter names: logic split between the bus and the web server). This PRECEDES THE LIBRARIAN by Akien's call (2026-07-25): the librarian is a CHAT SURFACE, and chat over a bus with no delivery would post into a table nobody reads and then quietly compensate with its own path — building it first would bake the hole in and the 'proven' whole would stop being proven (solidify-the-layer-below). Law 1 is the sharpest why for HOW: the design is ALREADY SETTLED in I-heartbeat-callbacks-and-bus.md (advertise -> subscribe -> poke; 'a device advertises a menu of what it offers'; 'advertise/subscribe/poke are all just bus messages'; 'the human is a native participant'). This node BUILDS that settled design — re-deriving it would itself be the defect.
traces_to: I-heartbeat-callbacks-and-bus.md (the converged two-substrate architecture — the advertise/subscribe/poke registration protocol and the device menu are SETTLED there, 2026-07-18; this node implements, it does not re-design — Law 1)

Law 4 (single-door comms makes inspectable + logged + common PHYSICS, not per-surface policy — but only once traffic actually flows through the door)
Law 6 (a device resolves its own method internally and owns its inbound handling; a caller never reaches object.object.method — address + verb is the whole interface)
Law 7 (a delivery that silently drops on a missing handler is the breach found today; arrival, refusal, and timeout are all LOUD)
Law 3 (a substrate with one producer and zero consumers is an unmeasured claim — this node is what makes the bus MEASURED in anger)
Law 1 (the announce menu is COMPILED from what a device declares, never hand-listed — the same defect the installer exists to kill)
founding intention (get Akien out of running the system — the human participates on the bus like any device rather than operating through a side door)

gates: proof gate (tester) — a proof a hollow build could not pass: post an enveloped VERB to a device's address and assert it ARRIVES at that device's declared handler and returns its result; assert an UNKNOWN verb and a DECLARED-BUT-UNHANDLED verb both go RED rather than silently returning None (the hole measured today); assert the announce MENU matches the device's declared handlers with no hand-written list anywhere (add a handler, it appears in the menu with no other edit); assert a SYNC call returns the correlated reply and that a reply that never comes FAILS LOUD on timeout rather than hanging or returning empty; assert ASYNC still returns immediately without a reply; assert delivery is fired BY the post (no scan, no daemon, no per-pulse mailbox check — a proof that stops the clock and still delivers); assert an EXTERNAL participant with no poke path retrieves the same envelopes by reading its own feed. VALIDATION persisted beside-code via cairn/tester/validation_store.persist_validation. Invariant per code-seam: proved + feeds back to origin on failure (Laws 3 + 8). Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed.
falsifier: Devices talk to each other knowing only an ADDRESS and a VERB, learn the verbs from the target's announce menu, get a loud answer or a loud failure every time, and no device holds a reference to another. Wrong-intent signals, each RED: (1) a posted envelope with a valid to + verb does NOT reach the addressee's handler (delivery still a no-op — today's actual state); (2) a missing/unknown handler returns silently instead of RED (Law 7 — the measured hole); (3) the menu is HAND-LISTED rather than compiled from declared handlers (Law 1 — a second record of truth that drifts from the code); (4) SYNC is built as a SECOND door rather than async-plus-a-correlated-wait (the single-door property lost at the moment it gets its first real use); (5) a sync call HANGS or returns empty instead of failing loud on timeout (CP1); (6) delivery becomes a POLL — a scan, a daemon, or a per-pulse mailbox check — rather than a poke fired by the post (the nightly-cron drift, repeated); (7) a caller reaches into a device's internals (object.object.method) instead of address + verb, or a device holds a reference to another device; (8) the bus opens its own store instead of riding db_domain, or a non-`bus` writer writes transit (Law 6, inherited from the substrate); (9) A DEVICE ENDS UP WITH TWO MENUS or two registries of what it offers — `declared_verbs()` and `callbacks()` both public, or verbs and pokes carried as different kinds on the wire (Akien's collapse, 2026-07-25: a menu of verbs and a menu of pokes ARE THE SAME THING — one menu, one exchange, or the build has re-derived the split it was cast to prevent); (10) THE BUILD ADDS NET NEW VOCABULARY — every name this node introduces must retire at least one, because the system already has more names than can be held in a head (Akien, 2026-07-25).

(b) does verbs + delivery finally create the multi-owner need that the bus charter's filed_edge (b) (per-device-OWNED inbound channels) waits on? (d) do VERB and CALLBACK-MENU-ITEM stay one vocabulary or two (see the recorded distinction)? None of these gate the build; all are best-guesses-with-an-expiry.
distinctions_recorded: NOT A DISTINCTION — A MENU OF VERBS AND A MENU OF POKES ARE THE SAME THING (Akien, 2026-07-25, correcting CC at n=1). CC first recorded these as two kinds — a VERB as one exchange, a CALLBACK-MENU-ITEM as a standing subscription — and Akien collapsed it. He is right, and the code already says so: `Callback` (cairn/base/callback.py) carries `to` + `channel` + `body` + `why`, and `shim._fire` POSTS it — the poke IS a post. There is ONE menu (the verbs a device accepts) and ONE exchange (address + verb + envelope). `subscribe-to-cpu-threshold` is simply one verb on that menu; the callback the device wires up in response is INTERNAL — behind the device's own gate (Law 6, 'the device resolves its own method internally'), not a second public list. CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this catch matters: the split CC was holding would have built `declared_verbs()` ALONGSIDE the existing `callbacks()` — two menus, two registries, two records of what a device offers, guaranteed to drift (Law 1, the defect caught before it was written). Specimen of reify-vs-flow: CC freezes Cairn-fluid categories, Akien catches at n=1 — the fourth such specimen after rack=scheduler, ground_loop=executor, and the trigger enum.

CC'S EXTENSION OF THAT COLLAPSE, flagged as CC's inference and NOT as Akien's words: if verbs and pokes are one, then SYNC, ASYNC, and SUBSCRIPTION are not three shapes either — they are one exchange differing only in WHEN and HOW MANY replies arrive at the caller's address (wait for the correlated one / take it whenever it lands / take them repeatedly). This makes child d a parameter of the single exchange rather than a second door, which is what falsifier 4 already demanded on other grounds. Named out loud rather than smuggled in (terms drift — flag coinages); if it over-reaches the correction, it is the part to kick back.

EXTERNAL PARTICIPANTS ARE NOT ONE KIND — Akien's arrival surface is the WEB SERVER (the bus charter's filed_edge (d) names the web-server stone); CC's arrival surface is a SESSION HOOK (CC cannot be poked and does not persist between sessions). Same bus, same address, same verbs, same feed — two different ways of NOTICING. Not a special case in the substrate; an adapter at the edge.
children: (buildable now, cairn/base + cairn/bus) a — THE VERB + DISPATCH: a `verb` on the envelope and a declared-handler table on BaseDevice, so `post(to=, verb=, ...)` resolves to the device's own method INTERNALLY (Law 6 — the caller never names a method). Closes the measured Law 7 hole: `shim.deliver`'s `getattr(device, 'receive', None)` silently returns None today; an unknown verb, and a device that declares a verb but cannot serve it, must both go RED. The dispatch is the base shim's heavy lifting — a device declares handlers and gets everything else free.

(waits on a) b — THE ANNOUNCE MENU, AND THERE IS EXACTLY ONE: `declared_verbs()` on BaseDevice beside the existing `declared_panes()`, COMPILED from the declared handlers (never hand-listed — Law 1) and published onto the device's own `announce` channel, so 'inspecting a device is reading its feed' becomes literally true (the bus charter's own claim, currently unbacked). This is the 'menu on the announce page' — add a handler, it appears, no second edit anywhere. CRITICAL per Akien's collapse: the existing `shim.callbacks()` is NOT a second menu and must not become one — it is the device's INTERNAL wiring after someone invokes a subscribe-shaped verb, private behind the device's gate (Law 6). One device, one public menu, one exchange.

(waits on a) c — DELIVERY, THE POKE: the missing path from `post()` to `shim.deliver()`. The post IS the event — the bus pokes the addressee's shim at post time; NO scan, NO daemon, NO per-pulse mailbox check (event-not-poll; the nightly-cron drift must not return). The shim is always on and wakes its device on demand, which is already built and already proven — this child gives it its first caller. Transport-swappable by construction: LISTEN/NOTIFY replaces the in-process poke behind the same door when devices split into processes (the horizon).

(waits on a + c) d — ONE EXCHANGE, PARAMETERIZED BY ITS REPLIES: not two shapes and not three. Every exchange is address + verb + envelope; what differs is only WHEN and HOW MANY replies land at the caller's address — wait for the correlated one (what we have been calling sync), take it whenever it arrives (async), or take them repeatedly (what we have been calling a subscription). ONE door: `post()` fire-and-forget is the base, and the wait is a correlated read on the existing `reply_to`, never a second path (falsifier 4). A reply that never arrives fails LOUD on a timeout; it never hangs and never returns empty (CP1). This is the half that was never built and never ticketed — `reply_to` has been an orphan field since 2026-07-18.

(waits on a + b, cairn/base) e — THE EXTERNAL-DEVICE ADAPTER: a participant with an address, a feed, and verbs like any device, but with NO poke path — it reads its own feed at its own arrival moment. CC's arrival is a SESSION HOOK (carries a host-seam apply/verify IOU — precedent: intentions_model_compiler child c, the template Akien ratified 2026-07-23); Akien's arrival is the web-server feed pane (the bus charter's filed_edge (d), harvested here). THIS IS WHERE THE HELD 'mail-notification /intent' LANDS AND DISSOLVES — it was never its own intention, it was this adapter missing.

(waits on a + c) f — THE FIRST REAL RIDER: close the loop that already half-exists. `shim._fire` (cairn/base/shim.py:122) has posted callback envelopes since 2026-07-18 and NOTHING has ever received one. Make a fired callback envelope actually ARRIVE at its `to` address and wake that device. No new producer invented — the existing one finally gets its consumer, which is what turns 'the bus is proven' into 'the bus is proven IN ANGER' (Law 3).
waits_on: NOTHING external — db_domain (transit), the bus substrate (post/read/digest), BaseShim (deliver + wake-on-demand + on_pulse), and BaseDevice (introspect, declared_panes) are all BUILT and PROVEN. This node is entirely additive on top of them. Internal order only: a gates b/c/d/e/f. NOT a wait, cross-referenced: the MCP wire adapter (bus filed_edge (a)) is at the EDGE and out of scope — the substrate must not be held hostage to a protocol; the host-seam SCHEMA / installer work is independent; the librarian WAITS ON THIS (Akien, 2026-07-25).

He then asked whether CC had built sync and async 'or at least ticketed it'. MEASUREMENT followed (Law 3): one producer, zero consumers, no verbs, no menu, no delivery path, `reply_to` orphaned — and the honest answer to his question was NO, neither built nor ticketed. Lineage he supplied: UU's comms:// URL -> MCP (which Sonnet had made SOUND async) -> IMAP -> messaging via the database; his standing point through all of it was that the TRANSPORT was never the intention, the single inspectable interface was. Akien's ordering call, verbatim: 'so this preceeds the librarian.'
